GRUB loading the kernel and initramfs and passing the kernel command line
The boot loader's whole job: find the kernel and initramfs, load them, pass the command line, and jump to the kernel.
systemd as process 1 starting the default target and its services
systemd is process 1. It reads its units and brings the machine up to the default target.
An admin using ipmitool over the network to the BMC for power, sensors and console
The BMC answers over the network even when the server is off. ipmitool is the client.
How apt gets a package from a repository mirror after checking its signature
Packages come from repositories listed in sources. apt update refreshes the list, and signatures are checked.
The common signals SIGTERM, SIGKILL, SIGHUP, SIGINT and SIGSTOP and what each does
Ask politely with SIGTERM first. SIGKILL cannot be caught.
Runnable processes waiting in a per-CPU run queue while the scheduler picks the next one
Each CPU has a run queue. The scheduler picks the next process and preempts when the time slice ends.
Cold anonymous pages moved from RAM to swap and back in when needed
Swap holds cold anonymous pages. Heavy swapping makes everything slow.
What lives in /proc and /proc/sys and how sysctl reads and writes kernel settings
/proc shows live kernel and process state. sysctl changes kernel settings under /proc/sys.
Which command shows which hardware: lscpu, lsblk, lspci, free, dmidecode
One command per question about the hardware.
A user running sudo, the sudoers check, then the command as root with a log entry
sudo checks the rules, runs the command as root, and leaves a log entry.
Permission bits r, w and x with the numbers 4, 2 and 1 and an example mode
Add the numbers per group. 7 is rwx, 5 is r-x, 4 is r only.
sar flags for CPU, memory, disk and network history
sar records history, so you can look at what happened an hour ago.
Three switches in a loop where Spanning Tree blocks one link
STP blocks one link so that frames cannot loop forever.
Destination NAT before routing and source NAT after routing on a Linux router
DNAT changes the destination before routing. SNAT and MASQUERADE change the source after routing.
The chain from kubelet through CRI, containerd, shim and runc to the container process
kubelet speaks CRI to containerd. containerd uses a shim and runc to start the container.
kubelet and containerd both needing the same systemd cgroup driver, set in two places
Set the same cgroup driver in the kubelet and in containerd, or the node becomes unstable.
A cgroup tree from the root through slices to a container with controllers
cgroups form a tree. Limits on a parent apply to everything below it.
The runtime calling a CNI plugin ADD that creates a veth, assigns an IP and returns a result
The runtime calls the CNI plugin with ADD. The plugin wires the network and returns the IP.
The Kubernetes network rules: every pod has its own IP and pods reach each other without NAT
Every pod gets its own IP. Pods reach each other directly with no NAT.
Overlay networking compared with native routing for pod networks
Overlay works anywhere but adds a header. Routed is leaner but the fabric must carry pod routes.
A client request through a load balancer and ingress controller to a Service and pods
Ingress sends HTTP traffic by host and path to Services.
How a volume is attached, formatted, mounted under the kubelet directory and bind-mounted into the container
The kubelet mounts the volume on the node first, then bind-mounts it into the container.
The upgrade order: etcd snapshot, first control plane node, other control planes, then workers one by one
Upgrade the control plane first, then each worker. Drain, upgrade, uncordon.
The API request pipeline: authentication, authorization, mutating admission, validation, then etcd
Every request passes authentication, authorization and admission before it is stored.
NFD and GFD labelling nodes so the GPU Operator knows where to run
NFD labels what the hardware is. GFD adds GPU details. The operator reads the labels.
The GPU Operator reading a ClusterPolicy and deploying its operands in order on GPU nodes
One ClusterPolicy tells the operator what to install on every GPU node, in order.
The TCP/IP path through the kernel compared with the RDMA path from NIC to memory
TCP goes through the kernel and CPU. RDMA lets the NIC move data straight to memory.
The three Pod Security Standards levels: privileged, baseline and restricted
Three levels. Restricted is the strictest and is the target for normal workloads.
